title: Captain Murray Accepts the Account Before the Shyam Singh Episode

blocks.text: The page returns to the moral charge sheet against Mughal rule by recalling the fate of The innocent Sahibzadas and the repeated assaults on the Guru and his household. These acts are not treated as isolated cruelties but as proof that Mughal power had forfeited any moral right to govern the Panth.

From there the author resumes the courtroom-like conclusion of the previous discussion. On every count had the Mughals been proved wrong, and in both the worlds had they been discredited by the evidence of persecution, sacrifice, and survival.

Captain David Murray then gives the account public weight. Fully did he believe in the narrator's version, saying it should be forwarded onward, even To the British Sovereign, the king of England, before the book turns to the opening of Shyam Singh's misl.
